content:
Rocco now has Scene.environment for setting the sky, the clear colour, the tone map, the exposure, fog and bloom.

https://github.com/Pixelsprout/rocco-engine/releases/tag/v0.10.0
@pixelsprout Do you have more example images anywhere? The image you just posted looks really nice!

@Steve Howell I'm working on a more detailed scene at the moment which has more detail. Includes ambient occlusion, batched draw calls, particle emitter, volumetric fog and more...

I'll probably do a blog post once I have worked through some benchmarks and testing.
Looks amazing!

By the way, I am cribbing a couple ideas from your tutorial for a tutorial that I am writing:

  • ending each chapter on what's still missing
  • opening with a short list of what's new
  • giving each interactive widget an instruction and a predicted result
  • a page of surprises

I particularly like the "surprises".

@pixelsprout I've been watching your progress on Rocco! I have two projects that will maybe kinda fit it.

One is a board game called FastTrack, which seems like an odd fit, but it actually lends itself to a simple 3D rendering of the table and the board with nice lighting effects. It's a game popular among the older crowd that I have played with my mom and her friends, and people sometimes build their own boards in a wood shop, so the game has a little culture of craftsmanship.

The more natural candidate is my Safari Ride screensaver, and I actually had Claude evaluate the synergy possibilities. Strangely, Rocco is TOO sophisticated for it. Part of the "charm" of my game is that a lot of it's kinda cartoonish, so even though the screensaver is a first-person 3D experience (I count it as true 3D because birds actually fly), it doesn't really demand much beyond basic trig for rendering.

I made the first step toward future integration, which is that I ported my own server from zig toward odin. I assume you're pretty happy with odin?
I have a lot of tokens to burn, so I may also just start another project to dip my toes into the water. Let me know if you have ideas for small things to build.

Simple rendering with a cartoon appearance should be possible, most of the advanced effects can be turned off and are off by default. You can also apply custom shaders to provide the look and feel you are after.

Yeah I'm happy with Odin, it's even simpler than Zig and has a ton of vendored libraries you can easily use. Odin also provides convenient built ins useful for game math, such as the matrix type - https://odin-lang.org/docs/overview/#matrix-type
Cool, I'm hoping to play with Rocco in a week or two after wrapping up a couple other projects.

Keen to hear any feedback you have. FYI I am often doing breaking changes as I try to find the right API.

Just make sure you switch to the roc nightly I have pinned for the project. I try to update the nightly version once a week so that I'm not too far behind.

http://143.244.172.148:9100/notes/rocco-engine-for-safari.md holds the notes from my most recent investigation, but it could very easily be out of date now, and it assumes some context about my Safari Ride app (see https://roc.lynrummy.com/tutorial/introduction.html and #contributing > a little Roc book). I think an agent could mostly grok it. If you prefer, I can have Claude write a more up-to-date analysis.

(One of our blockers was that we are already managing a lot of slightly different Roc versions across my other apps. It's not a true blocker; it was just one more detail that I wasn't ready to deal with at the time.)

This may be out of date, too, but it's a bug report:

http://143.244.172.148:9100/notes/rocco-first-contribution.md

These notes are all agent-written, in case it's not obvious haha.

That assessment is really helpful to me as I can see where there are clear gaps within the engine for supporting different applications. I like the idea of adding the Shapes to the vocabulary as this will enable us to generate more complex meshes.

If you add Shapes, that will certainly reduce the friction for me! The second half of the safari ride happens after the sun sets behind the mountains, and that's where I would probably start using real features from Rocco for lighting and stuff.

I think I may already mentioned this, but we did port our platform to odin on a branch, which might reduce friction.

https://github.com/showell/roc-apps/tree/master/canvas_apps/safari is under UPL. I don't know if there's anything worth scavenging from there, but I would be flattered if you did!

I should mention that my safari app and some other apps can also run under roc-ray from Luke Boswell. I think some synergy there could be a selling point.

I mostly target the web for my apps, but an older version of safari actually runs as my windows screensaver, so I would love if Rocco could do that as well, but that's pretty low on my list.

I can definitely explore adding Shapes at some point soon, I was thinking of adding something like this at some point as it's too limiting just supporting .glb for mesh data. If you are keen to help contribute to Rocco then feel free to submit PRs. As you know the engine is mostly built with the help of agents, I just try to make sure I maintain a level of understanding with how the engine works and what the overall design is.
Supporting wasm builds shouldn't be too difficult. The lower level application library I use Sokol supports this target.
Sounds good!
@Steve Howell would the goal of porting Safari to Rocco be to maintain the fake 3D effect with the sprite animals in 3D space, or would you want build 3D assets that replace these?

@pixelsprout I haven't figured out exactly what I would do, but I think it would be mostly about enriching the nighttime portion of the ride, as I mentioned earlier. But, yeah, it would be cool to have actual 3D elephants. When I initially worked with the agents to create 3D anatomy models for animals, they were really terrible.

I also might want the rider to actually go somewhere interior. Like a tavern or something. And that's where the visual experience can get a lot richer and demand more from an engine. On the wide open road I find my primitive drawing style kinda fun, because you want to feel the open space.
I'm reposting your image here. It's this kind of look and feel that I think would be fun for the second half of the ride:

They are still quite bad at it haha :sweat_smile:

The latest fable is a bit better, I've had more luck using the Trippo service and then cleaning the mesh up afterwards.

I'm curious if you have a particular game that you're trying to build. I have a strange relationship with video games. I've hardly played any. My mind works too slow for first-person shooters. The only time I was truly immersed in a game was Myst.

But I love the technical challenges of games. And I think Roc is so well suited for a pretty large class of games.

I do enjoy board and card games, and some of my show-and-tell examples show that. But they're generally hard to compete with the physical experience.
The above is mostly addressed to pixelsprout but I'm curious if other folks are thinking about games. We can rename the topic if this turns into a digression; I don't want to hijack the Rocco thread.
I have a game I'm slowly working on with my 4 year old, she is coming up with ideas haha. But also trying to prove the engine with different types of games.
That's amazing!
Can you give any spoilers?
I will say unicorns are involved :unicorn::rainbow:
haha nice!

I don't have kids, but I remember that my niece and nephew were extremely competitive when they were about that age. I remember my nephew beating me in some kind of "concentration" game. I did NOT let him win.

I used to be so competitive that I cried when my paper airplane could not fly further than my nephew's :smile:
